predecessor_rollback_is_not_valid_for_th.what_stella_0017_rollback_does: It DROPs the 7-arg complete (stella_0017_rollback:153) and the 10-arg settle (stella_0017_rollback:311), and restores the 5-arg settle as a NON-delegating function with a real body (stella_0017_rollback:169). Its postcondition at line 360 asserts the restored 5-arg form is NOT still a delegator.
predecessor_rollback_is_not_valid_for_th.why_it_is_wrong_after_0017b: It rolls back to the stella_0016 state, not to the stella_0017 state. Run after stella_0017b it would leave the 9-arg complete and 12-arg settle standing, and its own postcondition at line 321 - which refuses when a payload-carrying function is still installed and still callable - would ABORT. It fails closed rather than corrupting, which is correct behaviour and also proof that no valid rollback for stella_0017b exists at AS_OF_HEAD.

The rollback restores a DELEGATOR, never a second writer of the ledger. The guarantee is that the ledger holds ONE INSERT reached by two arities, and it holds in the rolled-back state too.
